forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Castle Point admits unquantified financial risk in housing enforcement policy
news_drafts.lead: Castle Point Council has adopted a housing enforcement policy that allows it to carry out remedial works on properties where landlords have breached safety standards, then recharged the costs to the responsible party. However, the council's own papers acknowledge "an unknown unquantified risk from the individuals not being able to pay," creating potential bad debts that could fall back on the council. The policy was approved without an estimate of this exposure, and the council asserts the policy requires no new budget provision, despite the admitted liability risk. The three-year policy covers 2026 to 2029.
news_drafts.paper_title: Item 9 Report: Private Sector Housing Enforcement and Civil Financial Penalties Policies 2026 to 2029 - 16/09/2026

findings.paper_title: Item 9 Report: Private Sector Housing Enforcement and Civil Financial Penalties Policies 2026 to 2029 - 16/09/2026
findings.headline: The council faces an unknown and unquantified financial risk if landlords cannot pay for works undertaken in default
findings.detail: The policy permits Castle Point to carry out remedial works ('works in default') to fix housing violations, with costs recharged to the responsible person. However, the policy explicitly states there is an 'unknown unquantified risk from the individuals not being able to pay.' This represents a potential bad debt exposure that is not reflected in the policy's assertion of 'no new budget requirements.'
findings.matters: A lender assessing council finances needs to understand unquantified financial exposures and potential bad debts that could impact council cash flow and reserves
findings.figures: Risk amount unknown and unquantified; no estimate provided
findings.quote: Should works in default be required, all costs incurred will then be recharged to the relevant individuals. There is an unknown unquantified risk from the individuals not being able to pay.

findings.paper_title: Item 8 Report: Treasury Management Update: First Quarter Stage - Audit & Governance Committee - 21/07/2026
findings.headline: Full-year investment income forecast maintained at £624k despite Q1 outperformance, reflecting expected lower reinvestment rates as base rate falls
findings.detail: Despite achieving £133k favorable variance in Q1, the council's full-year investment income forecast remains unchanged at £624k. Management expects investment balances to reduce during the remainder of the year and maturing investments to be reinvested at lower rates as the Bank of England continues reducing rates, with the next reduction to 3.50% forecast for September 2027. The unchanged forecast demonstrates prudent and realistic expectations management.
findings.matters: Demonstrates credible financial forecasting and disciplined expectations management; important to lenders and peer councils assessing actual cash flow outlook in a declining rate environment
findings.figures: £624k full-year forecast (unchanged from budget), Q1 earned £289k, next BoE rate cut to 3.50% forecast September 2027
findings.quote: despite the year to date upside, the forecast for investment interest receivable for the full year remains unchanged at £0.624m, in line with the approved budget. Investment balances are expected to reduce over the remainder of the year, and maturing investments are likely to be reinvested at lower rates as the Bank of England is expected to continue reducing interest rates

findings.paper_title: Item 8 Report: Treasury Management Update: First Quarter Stage - Audit & Governance Committee - 21/07/2026
findings.headline: Investment interest earned £289k to 30 June 2026, £133k above original estimate, at 4.15% average return against SONIA benchmark of 3.73%
findings.detail: The council's Q1 investment returns exceeded forecast, with outperformance driven by Money Market Funds' resilience despite base rate reductions to 3.75%, which have not been fully reflected in MMF yields. Additional strength came from local authority placements achieving average rates of 5.3%, significantly above both the base rate and MMF yields. The outperformance demonstrates effective treasury management execution in a falling rate environment.
findings.matters: Lenders assess councils' cash generation and financial management capability; peer finance directors monitor strategies for optimizing investment returns in a declining rate environment
findings.figures: £289k interest earned, £133k favorable variance, 4.15% average return vs 3.73% SONIA, 5.3% average on local authority placements
findings.quote: the Council has earned £0.289m in investment interest as at 30 June 2026, representing a favourable variance of £133,000 against the original estimate. This positive performance is primarily due to the continued strength of returns from Money Market Funds, which have remained resilient despite the Bank of England reducing the base rate to 3.75%. Unlike other investment instruments, Money Market Funds have not fully reflected the reduction in the base rate, enabling the Council to continue benefiting from relatively favourable returns

findings.paper_title: Item 14 Appendix A: Award of Contract to Convert Abbeyfield House, Chapel Lane, Hadleigh - Table 3 - 17/06/2026
findings.headline: General Fund savings reduced by £720k to £2,636k from original forecast of £3,356k
findings.detail: The scheme was originally forecast to generate £3,356k in savings to the General Fund but is now forecast at £2,636k, a reduction of £720k in expected financial benefit.
findings.matters: Reduced savings from a capital scheme affect its value for money and the council's budget position, influencing finance directors' assessments of whether to proceed with or reprioritise similar schemes.

findings.headline: Borrowing costs increased by £1,173k: interest up £352k and MRP up £821k
findings.detail: Interest costs increased from originally forecast £1,019k to revised £1,371k (up £352k). Minimum Revenue Provision increased from £1,900k to £2,721k (up £821k). These reflect the additional debt financing required for the cost overrun.
findings.matters: Additional borrowing and its annual servicing cost matter to lenders assessing debt levels and to finance directors managing revenue budget allocation for capital repayment.
